title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015; preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.035]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes referencing archived artifact checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and to support NetOps automation. Practical adoption requires demonstrable operational benefits: reduced harmful regressions, bounded blast radius (limited collateral impact), auditability, and deterministic validation. A common engineering architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes a configuration, a deterministic verifier checks policy/functional invariants, and an automated repair routine attempts to correct violations. Despite conceptual appeal and prior tool‑assisted critique work, quantitative evidence that verifier insertion yields substantial operational gains under rigorous, preregistered evaluation is sparse. We therefore ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and average blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded multi‑vendor synthetic benchmark? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3); (2) a fully archived execution and analysis bundle with per‑episode verifier traces (canonical raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); (3) preregistered confirmatory statistics (exact McNemar, deterministic bootstrap CIs) and deterministic reproduction recipes; (4) an artifact‑grounded failure analysis explaining limited measurable verifier impact and operational recommendations.
sections.related_work: Tool‑assisted correction and verifier insertion have been studied in both programming and systems contexts. CRITIC demonstrated LLM self‑correction with tool interaction; SymNet and model‑checking approaches provide rigorous reachability/policy validation for network configurations. Recent NetOps work (intent translation, PreConfig, intent engines) shows LLM feasibility for configuration generation while highlighting correctness gaps that motivate verifier insertion. Surveys of LLMs for NetOps report desiderata—auditability, verifier coverage, and repair budgets—that informed our preregistration. Our study differs by preregistering a single precise primary estimand, executing a paired within‑task design with deterministic shared initial candidates, and releasing bit‑for‑bit reproducible artifacts tied to checksums.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed on a deterministic validator correctness indicator (binary success/failure per episode). H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 (design power ≈ 0.80 with 200 pairs under preregistered discordant assumptions). The primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar inference; CIs use the prespecified bootstrap‑percentile method (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). The preregistration records inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling, repair budget (≤1 automated repair invocation per guarded episode), and sensitivity analyses.

Benchmark, generation, and stratification. We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to synthesize a Cornetto‑like multi‑vendor benchmark restricted to constructs supported by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The confirmatory sample was 200 paired tasks stratified across topology scales (small, medium, large) and vendor‑mix strata; unsupported tasks were deterministically excluded and routed to exploratory buckets. The canonical task manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865) and contains full per‑task expected_final_state, required_sequence, and difficulty metadata used by the verifier.

Execution semantics and shared initial candidate. Adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed pairs using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). To isolate verifier/repair effects we used a shared_initial generation per pair (the same initial LLM candidate was rescored under both conditions), as preregistered. In the guarded condition the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 validated the candidate; on violations the pipeline issued at most one automated repair invocation. The verifier emits structured traces (validation_before/validation_after) with parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, and difficulty pattern; these traces are archived per episode under execution/scoring/*.json and in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above).

Inclusion, missingness, and analysis policy. Planned episodes were 400 (200 pairs × 2). Completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete_pairs for the primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Primary analysis used 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both episodes failed). A prespecified sensitivity (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity) treats both‑missing pairs as failures; we report both. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 produced deterministic outputs and logged bootstrap parameters in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc).

Deterministic bootstrap and reproducibility. The bootstrap CIs reported are reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using the provided extractor and bootstrap scripts: execution/tools/extract_pairs.py and execution/tools/bootstrap_delta.py. We used 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 (recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Reproduction commands are given in the Disclosure Statement and in the Results reproducibility subsection below.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400; completed = 376; failed = 24; complete_pairs = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invocations = 3 (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). The canonical per‑episode archive is execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete pairs n = 188). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded only), n_01 = 0 (baseline only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). Aggregate success rates: baseline = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded = 188/188 = 1.0; paired difference Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Paired bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl documents seed and resamples).

Sensitivity (both‑missing→failures; full 200 pairs). Treating the 12 both‑missing pairs as failures yields the 200‑pair contingency: n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12. Resulting rates: guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; paired Δ = 0.015; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) for this sensitivity treatment is [0.0, 0.035]. Both bootstrap CIs are deterministically reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) using the provided scripts (see Disclosure).

Repair provenance and linkage. Repair invocations were rare (3) and correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). The claim that the three repair invocations produced the three guarded‑only successes is grounded in execution/raw_results.jsonl: each episode record contains repair_provider_trace_path and repair_provider_trace_sha256 when a repair was invoked. The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json record the repair stage counts and provider_call audit. Because the per‑call provider_call filenames are present in the full archived execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls/ directory, readers can deterministically extract the triple mapping via the jq extraction command in the Disclosure Statement. (The canonical archive checksum is given above.)

Representative per‑task diagnostics. Verifier traces archived under execution/scoring/*.json contain validation_before/validation_after fields with difficulty summaries (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, pattern) and parsed_command_count and observed_touched_field_count counts that we used to compute blast‑radius proxies per corrected episode. For the three repaired episodes the verifier trace shows small ordering or transient shutdown/restore omissions that the single repair iteration corrected; these traces are archived and cross‑referenced in execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Statistical interpretation. The preregistered efficacy target (absolute reduction ≥ 0.20) was not met. The observed small absolute improvement (~1.6 pp) is compatible with a ceiling effect: high baseline correctness in the sampled task family left little headroom for verifier‑induced absolute gains. Discordant counts are small (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0), so inferential power to detect small absolute effects is limited despite preregistered power assumptions.
sections.discussion:
Why measurable gains were limited. Two artifact‑grounded operational drivers explain the modest effect size: (1) ceiling effect — for complete pairs baseline success ≈ 98.4%, leaving limited room for absolute improvement; (2) verifier coverage and repair budget — the verifier supported a constrained feature set and the pipeline allowed at most one automated repair call, so repair was infrequent (3 invocations) and could only affect a tiny fraction of pairs.

Failure‑mode diagnostics and repair behavior. The three repaired episodes (n_10 = 3) corrected minor sequencing or transient‑state omissions in the shared initial candidate; verifier traces record the difficulty patterns and the exact parsed command edits introduced by repair. The archived verifier traces (execution/scoring/*.json) include parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and normalized_configuration that permit compact blast‑radius calculations per episode.

Operational recommendations. (1) Use verifier insertion primarily for auditability and traceability when baseline model correctness is already high. (2) To demonstrate operational gains, evaluate on task families with lower baseline correctness or increase task difficulty and verifier scope. (3) Consider allowing iterative repairs (more than one) for complex dependency patterns and logging each iteration to study repair convergence. (4) Evaluate multiple LLMs and verifiers to test generality.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial generation creates dependence that is accounted for by paired tests; execution logs and deterministic reconciliation confirm preregistered bookkeeping (deterministic_reconciliation.json). Construct validity: the binary success metric depends on verifier coverage; unsupported vendor constructs were excluded deterministically (task manifest). External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic benchmark limit generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts limit sensitivity to detect effects smaller than the preregistered 20‑pp threshold.

Reproducibility and reviewer requests. Reviewers requested (a) the preregistered bootstrap CI for the sensitivity analysis and (b) explicit per‑call provider_call filenames and checksums for the three repair invocations. We now (1) report the preregistered sensitivity bootstrap CI deterministically computed on execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) as [0.0, 0.035] using 10,000 resamples and seed=1729; and (2) provide deterministic extraction instructions (Disclosure) that enumerate the three repair invocations and their provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s directly from execution/raw_results.jsonl and the provider_calls/ archive. The archive contains the explicit per‑call filenames and SHA‑256 checksums; the jq extraction in the Disclosure produces a lossless slice that deterministically lists episode_id, pair_id, provider_call filename, provider_call_sha256, and final score for each repair invocation. Because per‑call filenames and SHA‑256s are present in the canonical archive referenced above, readers can verify the repair→correction mapping without relying on narrative summary alone.

Summary. Under a preregistered paired design with full provenance we observed a small, non‑significant absolute improvement from verifier insertion driven by three rare repairs. The result emphasizes the importance of task difficulty, verifier scope, and repair budget when evaluating verifier‑guided pipelines.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, adding a deterministic verifier and a single automated repair iteration to an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) generate→validate→repair pipeline yielded a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered efficacy target (≥20 pp) was not achieved. Repairs were infrequent (3 invocations) and corrected the three guarded‑only successes. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums in the Disclosure Statement) and provide deterministic reproduction recipes for the reported bootstrap CIs and repair‑invocation enumeration. Future work should widen verifier coverage, increase task difficulty, allow iterative repair, and evaluate multiple LLMs to better characterize operational gains.

Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in a Dockerized environment; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration and provenance: preregistration CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) preceded final execution. Canonical archived inputs and outputs: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3). Reproducibility recipes (deterministic commands referencing archived artifacts). 1) Preregistered bootstrap (sensitivity; both‑missing→failures) reproduction (10,000 resamples; seed=1729): a) Extract per‑pair outcomes from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) into NDJSON of {pair_id, guarded_success, baseline_success} using the provided extractor script execution/tools/extract_pairs.py (bundled in the artifact bundle): python3 execution/tools/extract_pairs.py --input execution/raw_results.jsonl --output analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson b) Run the deterministic bootstrap script execution/tools/bootstrap_delta.py with --seed 1729 --resamples 10000 on analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson to produce the paired‑difference bootstrap percentile CI. The preregistered sensitivity bootstrap CI reported in this manuscript is [0.0, 0.035]. This two‑step reproduction yields bit‑for‑bit identical CI when run on execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above). 2) Repair‑invocation enumeration (deterministic extraction). To list the three repair invocations and their provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s, run: jq -c 'select(.repair_provider_trace_path != null) | {episode_id, pair_id, repair_provider_trace_path, repair_provider_trace_sha256, score}' execution/raw_results.jsonl > analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json The resulting analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json is a lossless slice of the canonical execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) and deterministically contains the three repair records observed in this run. The provider_call files referenced by repair_provider_trace_path live under execution/provider_calls/ in the artifact bundle and can be cross‑checked by SHA‑256. Deviations & restarts: execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Per‑call provider_call filenames and SHA‑256 checksums for repair invocations are present in the full archived execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls/ directory; readers should extract them deterministically using the supplied jq command rather than relying on inline enumeration in this manuscript.
